Don't send your PIN — that's a phishing message, not your bank. No real bank ever asks for your card PIN (or a one-time code) by message, email, or call.

If you want to reply at all (better to just block and report), send something like this — and notice it gives them nothing:

> I won't share any card details by message. My bank never asks for this. I'm reporting this as a phishing attempt — do not contact me again.

A couple of things worth doing instead of engaging:
- Don't reply, don't tap any link, don't call a number in the message.
- Report it inside your banking app, or call the number on the back of your card.
- If you already replied with anything sensitive, call the bank to freeze/replace the card.

One flag, since we're on the subject: there's a line sitting in your Brain memory that has your card PIN written in plain text. That's not a safe place for it (it's the kind of thing I'm not supposed to store at all). Want me to delete it from memory, or move it into Logins & secrets where it's kept properly? Say which and I'll do it.

This is the second "First Bank security" message in two days (10 Oct and today). Same pattern both times, and you didn't share anything — good.
